articles.title: How Gulf states are refinancing sovereign wealth funds as Iran war hits revenues
articles.summary:
How Gulf states are refinancing sovereign wealth funds as Iran war hits revenues

Submitted by Ahmed Alqarout on Wed, 09/30/2026 - 17:27
A small group of US and Canadian firms now sit across Gulf energy infrastructure and money, as the boundaries between sovereign wealth and private capital are breaking down
The logo for Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund is pictured during an event in Indian Wells, California, on 13 March 2024 (Matthew Stockman/Getty Images/AFP)
Off

Four Gulf states have rewritten the mandates of their main sovereign wealth funds since January. Officials have presented each change as long-planned institutional maturity. 

Not one has mentioned the Iran war, but wartime financial pressure signals the changes are being driven by fiscal recalculations as well. 

The restructuring accelerates a prewar trend. Since October 2023, Gulf funds have been cutting back spending and shifting towards narrower revenue-generating activities, as global geopolitical turmoil has driven up costs.

In July, the state-owned Kuwait Oil Company put its crude pipeline network into a joint venture with US investment funds Blackstone and KKR, and Canada's Brookfield. The $16bn deal left the Kuwaiti side holding a 51 percent stake and leasing 13 pipelines back for 20.5 years, in exchange for a volume-based tariff. Kuwait took $7.85bn upfront.

Kuwait spent the rest of the year building the law around deals like this, with new economic courts, an amended capital markets statute, and a plan to rewrite a quarter of its legislation by December. 

A few weeks ago, Kuwait issued a decree to let the treasury borrow from the Future Generations Fund, the pot set aside for the generation after oil. The 1976 law that created it had banned withdrawals outright. 

Borrowing is now capped at a tenth of the fund’s net assets, recorded as a debt owed back and repayable once the budget returns to surplus.

Engine of growth

Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, ran a deficit of 160 billion riyals ($42.6bn) in the first half of the year - its worst since 2016. The Public Investment Fund (PIF) was once filled by the state from oil receipts, but there is less to give now, so it raises its own funding. 

The PIF sold $2bn of sukuk, a type of financial certificate, in January, and a record $7bn of bonds in May, for which investors bid around $29bn. The money ultimately goes into companies owned by the PIF, which return some of it as dividends and taxes to state coffers.

The pressure is not expected to ease. The ministry's pre-budget statement for 2027 projects a deficit of 190 billion riyals ($50bn), around 3.6 percent of GDP, to be met by further borrowing and by what it calls alternative financing through project finance, infrastructure finance and export credit agencies.

The PIF recently ordered spending cuts across more than 100 of its companies, slowing projects and laying people off, months before the board approved its 2026-30 plan this past April, splitting the fund into three portfolios named Vision, Strategic and Financial. The plan describes the fund moving from being the primary engine of growth to the steward of platforms that let others scale, while it facilitates borrowing and foreign investment.

The funds are betting that the new borrowing will at least push the financial strain temporarily away, while new investment revenues come in before outstanding bills are due

In September, PIF executives reportedly flew to New York with representatives from the AI firm Humain, the King Abdullah Financial District, and real-estate developer Red Sea Global, where they were set to meet investors from mega funds Apollo, Blackstone, Brookfield, Carlyle, KKR, Stonepeak and the US Export-Import Bank. 

The Saudis were reportedly looking for foreign backing amid cash constraints at home. Three of those firms had bought Kuwait’s pipelines two months earlier.

For Qatar, companies at home are losing their earning power, and a fund that holds them is more expensive to borrow against. On 20 September, the prime minister carved roughly one-third out of the $580bn sovereign fund into a platform called Doha Investment, holding more than 40 companies, including Qatar Airways and Qatar National Bank. 

Its job is to back national champions, deepen capital markets and bring in international capital. It opened with a $60bn pipeline of opportunities, with $38.5bn in infrastructure projects, including public-private partnerships.

Separated, each half carries its own risk profile. Lenders and investors now price Doha Investment on its own rather than against the whole fund, which lets Qatar borrow against its strongest assets on better terms and bring partners into the weaker ones.

Boundaries dissolving

Earlier in 2026, Abu Dhabi folded its wealth fund ADQ, worth $263bn, into a new vehicle called L’imad, with $300bn and more than 250 group subsidiary companies. In July, it brought in Boston Consulting Group and started calling itself an operationally active shareholder, rather than an investor. 

Last week, Bloomberg reported that L’imad was preparing to raise money from outside investors for a unit being built to back private equity funds and make its own deals.

The funds have not stopped their outside deals, but refocused them. Earlier in September, the US Federal Communications Commission cleared the way for 49.5 percent foreign ownership of Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros Discovery. Of that, three Gulf funds would hold 38.5 percent of non-voting equity: PIF with 15.1 percent, L’imad with 12.8 and the Qatar Investment Authority with 10.6. The deal has not closed, and litigation could push completion into 2027. 

Has US war on Iran killed the 'Gulf moment'?
Read More »

Days later, Qatar signed a memorandum with JPMorgan Asset Management for a $20bn partnership, $5bn of it lending to mid-sized American firms. JPMorgan then helped to arrange the Qatari state’s own $3bn bond issuance. 

A small group of American and Canadian firms now sit across Gulf energy infrastructure and Gulf money at the same time, lending against assets they will not operate while managing the cash those assets generate. The funds were built to hold what oil earned, and are now being run to earn what oil no longer does, while holding up budgets and state-owned companies.

Slowly, the boundaries between sovereign wealth, fiscal financing and private capital are breaking down. The funds are betting that the new borrowing will at least push the financial strain temporarily away, while new investment revenues come in before outstanding bills are due. 

If so, the Gulf will have financed its transition with other people’s money, kept its savings, and come out with deeper capital markets and companies run to a standard outsiders are willing to pay for.

Yet a struggling global economy may fail to deliver expected results. If revenues and borrowing do not pick up fast enough, these states will have less room to manoeuvre, and Gulf citizens will likely foot the bill in their livelihoods, which may increase social strains. Social spending cuts, higher taxes and an overall decline in quality of life would follow.

articles.title: Iranian press review: 80m barrels behind oil minister’s resignation
articles.summary:
Iranian press review: 80m barrels behind oil minister’s resignation

Submitted by MEE correspondent on Thu, 10/08/2026 - 09:56
Meanwhile, an analyst says US withdrawal from Iraq could disadvantage Iran, tighter western immigration rules push Iranians towards China and Russia, and Armenia emerges as a key trade partner
The Iranian-flagged cargo ship Nora Bandar Abbas docked at the port of Umm Qasr in southern Iraq on 17 September 2026 (AFP)
Off

Minister falls victim to oil brokers network

Local media have linked Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad’s resignation on Sunday to growing tensions over the role of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) security figures in the national oil industry, as Iran faces difficulties selling its oil amid international sanctions and a US naval blockade.

Local media had previously reported that a group of four oil brokers close to senior IRGC security officials had been tasked with selling 80 million barrels of Iranian oil at discounted prices.

Officials denied the reports, while Paknejad’s resignation was attributed to personal reasons. But on Tuesday, the Saazandegi daily said pressure over the sale of the 80 million barrels was the main reason for his resignation.

According to Saazandegi, tensions arose between Paknejad and President Masoud Pezeshkian during one of the last cabinet meetings the oil minister attended.

'During war, sanctions and blockade, who is going to sell Iran’s oil, and who will oversee the oil brokers?'

- Saazandegi daily

The daily said the "growing power of the oil sales intermediary network", "uncertainty over the collection of oil revenues placed in its hands", and "parliament and oversight bodies becoming involved in investigating the oil brokers' activities" were among the factors that forced Paknejad to resign.

Saazandegi also addressed a question that has increasingly circulated in Iran over the past month: where is the money from the country’s oil sales?

Describing the difficulties Iran faces in selling oil and bringing the proceeds back into the country, the daily said Paknejad’s resignation had created a new problem for the sector.

“Now the question ‘Where is the oil money?’ has given way to a bigger question,” Saazandegi wrote. “During war, sanctions and blockade, who is going to sell Iran’s oil, and who will oversee the oil brokers?"

Meanwhile, Abdolhossein Hemmati Saraparde, deputy head of parliament’s energy commission, told the economic daily Donya-e Eqtesad that parliament was investigating contracts to sell Iranian oil.

He acknowledged that even the oil minister was unaware of the details of some contracts arranged to sell oil to China.

“The investigation and reviews are under way, but it is not yet possible to identify a specific person as responsible or determine the extent of any violations,” Saraparde said.

US exit from Iraq may hurt Iran in short term

Nozar Shafiei, a Tehran University academic, has suggested that the withdrawal of American forces from Iraq could work against Iran’s interests as the war with the US continues.

Iranian press review: Iranian elite profit billions from oil sanctions
Read More »

Shafiei, an international relations analyst, said the US withdrawal had been planned in advance, partly because of the costs of maintaining forces in Iraq and partly because of Iraqi opposition to their presence.

But he argued that the departure of US forces would also remove them from the reach of Iran and Iran-aligned groups in Iraq.

“The presence of these forces was an Achilles’ heel for the US in Iraq and imposed limitations on Washington in dealing with Iran,” Shafiei was quoted as saying by the Etemad newspaper.

According to Shafiei, the withdrawal of US forces could therefore take them out of Iran’s reach in Iraq while also removing American troops from the battlefield.

He concluded that while the withdrawal might benefit Iran in the long term, it could be damaging to it in the short term.

Iranians look east as western migration routes become harder

Iranians are increasingly looking to China and Russia as rising foreign-exchange costs and tighter immigration rules in western countries make traditional destinations harder to access, the Haft-e Sobh daily reported.

China is becoming a growing destination for Iranian students and technical professionals, particularly those with experience working on Chinese projects in Iran.

US sparks criticism after halting student visa appointments and extending ‘social media vetting’
Read More »

Russia is also attracting Iranians, including businesspeople, through its foreign investment programmes. Both countries are offering alternatives as access to western destinations becomes more difficult for Iranian applicants.

The shift is also affecting Iranian students, who in previous years were among the largest groups applying to universities in western countries but are increasingly looking towards China and Russia as established routes become harder to access.

Migration expert Saeed Salari told Haft-e Sobh that nationality plays a significant role in visa and employment applications, with Iranian applicants facing greater scrutiny in western countries.

He said the falling value of Iran’s currency has also made migration unaffordable for many Iranians, pushing those still able to leave toward cheaper and geographically closer destinations.

The daily added that Turkey and Armenia had also gained prominence among Iranians as regional alternatives for migration.

Tehran seeks to expand ties with Yerevan

Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan's visit to Tehran on Monday and his meetings with the Iranian president and foreign minister have fuelled speculation that Iran is seeking to expand overland trade through Armenia.

Can Baghdad gain control over paramilitary groups amid US war on Iran?
Read More »

Iran has faced serious disruptions to imports and exports in recent months due to the US naval blockade, prompting Tehran to turn to road and rail links with neighbouring countries.

On Tuesday, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi posted a video on Instagram of his meeting with Mirzoyan and said the talks focused on “the expanding relations between Tehran and Yerevan and ways to deepen cooperation in the economic, trade, transport, energy and other areas of interest to the two countries”.

Farsi media have also highlighted the geopolitical and economic importance of Iran’s land border with Armenia amid the US blockade.

The news website Fararu wrote that “relations with Yerevan are not merely a bilateral matter, but part of a policy to preserve Iran’s access to the Caucasus and maintain the importance of its transport routes in the region”.

The meeting also carries significance in the context of the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict between Armenia and Azerbaijan. 

Tehran and Yerevan have moved closer as Azerbaijan has expanded its military and intelligence cooperation with Israel in recent years, a development that has contributed to closer ties between the two countries.

*Iranian press review is a digest of news reports not independently verified as accurate by MEE.

Morning update

Good morning Middle East Eye readers,

Here are the latest developments: 

  • US President Donald Trump said that his special envoy Steve Witkoff is "doing very well" in discussions with Iran, but added that a deal with Tehran is not his preferred outcome. Trump also expressed that he expects the war on Iran to end soon, saying: "That war ends - it's going to be very soon. archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Rudém moři a okolí Hormuzského průlivu zůstává kritická kvůli sérii útoků na komerční tankery a plánované saúdské ofenzívě proti Houthiům. Navzdory tomu, že dodávky ropy se částečně stabilizovaly díky obchchvácení tras, globální námořní logistika trpí přetížením a přetrvávajícími vojenskými riziky.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and around the Strait of Hormuz remains critical due to a series of attacks on commercial tankers and a planned Saudi offensive against the Houthis. Although oil supplies have partially stabilized via alternative routing, global maritime logistics suffer from congestion and ongoing military risks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává zahájení saúdskoarabské ofenzívy v Jemenu a pokračující útoky v Hormuzském průlivu, což udrží vysokou volatilitu cen komodit a napětí v námořní dopravě.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the launch of the Saudi-led offensive in Yemen and ongoing attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are expected, keeping commodity price volatility and maritime transit tensions high.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se nadále vyhsoce prudce vyostřuje. Húsíové zintenzivnili útoky v oblasti Bab al-Mandeb a Hormuzského průlivu, kde jsou napadány komerční tankery, zatímco Saúdská Arábie připravuje rozsáhlou vojenskou ofenzívu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region continues to escalate sharply. Houthi rebels have intensified attacks in the Bab al-Mandeb and the Strait of Hormuz targeting commercial tankers, while Saudi Arabia is preparing a large-scale military offensive.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech se očekává spuštění avizované saúdské ofenzívy v Jemenu a pokračující útoky na tankery v Hormuzském průlivu, což udrží volatilitu komodit na vysoké úrovni.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the launch of the announced Saudi offensive in Yemen and continued tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz are expected, keeping commodity volatility elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabsky podporovaná jemenské vládní síly zahájily rozsáhlou ofenzívu proti Houthiům, zatímco v oblasti Rudého moře a Adenského zálivu nadále dochází k útokům na tankery. Navzdory eskalaci konfliktů se globální exporty ropy úspěšně přizpůsobují a díky alternativním trasám a vojenské asistenci víceméně obnovily předválečné objemy.
archive.security_status_en: Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces have launched a major offensive against the Houthis, while tanker attacks continue in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden region. Despite the escalating conflict, global oil exports have successfully adapted, rebounding to near pre-war volumes thanks to alternative routes and military assistance.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování rozsáhlých střetů v Jemenu a diplomatická jednání v Rijádu, což udrží napětí v oblasti na vysoké úrovni bez okamžitého dopadu na ropné toky.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, heavy clashes in Yemen and diplomatic talks in Riyadh are expected to continue, keeping regional tensions elevated without an immediate disruption to oil flows.

archive.security_status_cs: V Jemenu probíhá rozsáhlá ofenzíva mezinárodně uznané vlády a saúdskoarabské koalice s cílem získat zpět území ovládaná Houthi, včetně strategického pobřeží a průlivu Bab al-Mandab. Navzdory těmto bojům zůstávají globální dodávky ropy a toky přes klíčové trasy stabilní díky vojenské asistenci a alternativním trasám.
archive.security_status_en: A large-scale offensive is underway in Yemen by the internationally recognized government and the Saudi-led coalition to reclaim Houthi-held territory, including the strategic coastline and Bab al-Mandab strait. Despite these intense clashes, global oil supplies and flows through critical chokepoints remain stable thanks to military assistance and alternative routing.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování vojenské ofenzívy jemenské vlády a střetů v oblasti Bab al-Mandab, což udrží geopolitické napětí vysoké, avšak bez přímého dopadu na globální ropné toky.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the Yemeni government's military offensive and clashes around Bab al-Mandab are expected to continue, keeping geopolitical tensions high but without a direct impact on global oil flows.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou vojenskou ofenzívu a masivní leteckou kampaní čítající 100 stíhaček dobyla zpět přístav Mocha a oblast úžiny Bab al-Mandab. Konflikt eskaluje formováním nových regionálních aliancí (Makkah Alliance s podporou Pákistánu a Turecka) a hrozbou přímých odvetných útoků Houthiů.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive and a massive air campaign involving 100 fighter jets, recapturing the port of Mocha and the Bab al-Mandab strait area. The conflict is escalating with the formation of new regional alliances (Makkah Alliance with Pakistan and Turkey) and threats of direct Houthi retaliatory attacks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování saúdskoarabské letecké kampaně a pozemních střetů v oblasti Sanaá a Tihamah, což udrží vysokou nervozitu na trzích.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the continuation of the Saudi-led air campaign and ground clashes around Sanaa and Tihamah is expected, keeping market nervousness high.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou leteckou a pozemní operaci s cílem vytlačit Hútíje z pobřeží Rudého moře a zajistit strategickou úžinu Bab al-Mandab. Přestože globální dodávky ropy vykazují odolnost díky alternativním trasám, eskalace konfliktů a vojenská mobilizace Turecka a Pákistánu zvyšují geopolitické napětí v regionu.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition has launched a massive air and ground offensive to push the Houthis out of the Red Sea coast and secure the strategic Bab al-Mandab strait. Although global oil supplies show resilience due to alternative routes, escalating conflicts and the military mobilization of Turkey and Pakistan heighten regional geopolitical tensions.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování saúdskoarabské letecké a pozemní ofenzivy v Jemenu, což bude udržovat vysokou ostražitost na trzích s ropou a v oblasti námořní dopravy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the continuation of the Saudi-led air and ground offensive in Yemen is expected to maintain high vigilance in the oil and maritime shipping markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou leteckou a pozemní ofenzivu v Jemenu s cílem vytlačit hútíjské povstalce ze strategických oblastí kolem úžiny Bab al-Mandab. Do regionu se navíc chystá rychlé nasazení vojenských sil Turecka a Pákistánu na podporu Saúdské Arábie, což eskaluje napětí v oblasti Rudého moře.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition has launched a major air and ground offensive in Yemen aimed at dislodging Houthi rebels from strategic areas around the Bab al-Mandab strait. Furthermore, the planned rapid deployment of military forces from Turkey and Pakistan to support Saudi Arabia is escalating tensions in the Red Sea region.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování saúdskoarabské letecké ofenzivy v Jemenu a posilování vojenské přítomnosti spojenců v regionu, což bude udržovat vysokou ostražitost na trzích s ropou a v oblasti námořní dopravy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the continuation of the Saudi-led air offensive in Yemen and the strengthening of allied military presence in the region are expected to maintain high vigilance in the oil and maritime shipping markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou leteckou a pozemní ofenzivu 'Úsvit Jemenu' s cílem vytlačit hútíjské povstalce ze strategického pobřeží Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab. Do regionu se navíc chystají rychlé nasadit své síly Turecko a Pákistán v rámci obranného paktu, což eskaluje napětí.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition has launched a broad air and ground offensive 'Dawn of Yemen' aimed at dislodging Houthi rebels from the strategic Red Sea coastline and the Bab al-Mandab strait. Additionally, Turkey and Pakistan are moving to rapidly deploy forces to the region under a defense pact, escalating tensions.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování saúdskoarabské letecké a pozemní ofenzivy v Jemenu a diplomaticko-vojenské manévry spojenců, což udrží vysokou ostražitost na trzích s ropou.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the continuation of the Saudi-led air and ground offensive in Yemen and allied diplomatic-military maneuvers are expected to keep vigilance high in the oil markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou leteckou a pozemní ofenzivu v Jemenu s cílem vytlačit Hútíje z klíčových oblastí pobřeží Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab. Hútíové reagují odvetnými útoky včetně raketových úderů na letiště v Rijádu a vyhlášením saúdského vzdušného prostoru za otevřený cíl.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-led coalition launched a major air and ground offensive in Yemen aimed at dislodging the Houthis from key Red Sea coastal areas and the Bab al-Mandab strait. The Houthis are responding with retaliatory strikes, including missile attacks on Riyadh's airport and declaring Saudi airspace an open target.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování intenzivní saúdskoarabské letecké kampaně a pozemních bojů v Jemenu, doprovázené snahami Hútíovců o odvetné útoky.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, intensive Saudi-led air campaigns and ground fighting in Yemen are expected to continue, accompanied by Houthi efforts to launch retaliatory attacks.

archive.security_status_cs: Konflikt v Jemenu a okolí Rudého moře eskaluje do otevřené války. Saúdskou koalicí vedená letecká kampaň a ofenzíva proti Hútíovcům se střetávají s odvetnými útoky rebelů včetně úderů na saúdská letiště a vyhlášení saúdského vzdušného prostoru za otevřený cíl.
archive.security_status_en: The conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea region is escalating into an all-out war. The Saudi-led coalition's air campaign and offensive against the Houthis are meeting with retaliatory rebel strikes, including attacks on Saudi airports and the declaration of Saudi airspace as an open target.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování intenzivních bojů a leteckých úderů v Jemenu, přičemž Hútíové pravděpodobně zintenzivní snahy o odvetné útoky na saúdskou infrastrukturu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, intensive fighting and airstrikes in Yemen are expected to continue, with the Houthis likely stepping up retaliatory attacks on Saudi infrastructure.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Bab al-Mandabu se prudce vyhrotila poté, co saúdsky podporované vládní síly zahájily rozsáhlou ofenzívu proti Hútíům. V odvetě hnutí Hútí provádí raketové a dronové útoky na saúdská letiště a ropná zařízení Aramco, což zvyšuje riziko přímého regionálního konfliktu a ohrožuje svobodu plavby.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait has escalated sharply after Saudi-backed government forces launched a major offensive against the Houthis. In retaliation, the Houthi movement is launching missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports and Aramco oil facilities, heightening the risk of direct regional conflict and threatening freedom of navigation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračování rozsáhlé vládní ofenzívy v Jemenu podpořené nálety koalice, na což Hútíové odpoví dalšími asymetrickými útoky na saúdskou infrastrukturu. Napětí v oblasti Rudého moře a úžiny Bab al-Mandab zůstane na kritické úrovni.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the large-scale government offensive in Yemen backed by coalition airstrikes is expected to continue, prompting the Houthis to respond with further asymmetric attacks on Saudi infrastructure. Tension in the Red Sea and the Bab al-Mandab strait will remain at a critical level.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v oblasti Rudého moře a Perského zálivu zůstává kritická kvůli probíhajícím útokům Hútíů na letiště a ropnou infrastrukturu, jakož i úderům námořních dronů na tankery. Saúdskoarabská koalice zahájila rozsáhlou vojenskou ofenzívu s cílem vytlačit povstalce a obnovit kontrolu nad klíčovými námořními trasami.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the Red Sea and Persian Gulf remains critical due to ongoing Houthi attacks on airports and oil infrastructure, as well as naval drone strikes on tankers. The Saudi-led coalition has launched a major military offensive aimed at pushing back insurgents and regaining control over key maritime routes.
archive.forecast_cs: V následujících dnech se očekává eskalace saúdskoarabské ofenzívy v Jemenu, což vyvolá další asymetrické reakce Hútíů. Bezpečnostní rizika v Rudém moři a Hormuzském průlivu zůstanou extrémně vysoká.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, the Saudi-led offensive in Yemen is expected to escalate, prompting further asymmetric responses from the Houthis. Security risks in the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz will remain extremely high.

archive.security_status_cs: Saúdskoarabská ofenzíva v Jemenu a eskalující útoky Hútíů na Aden a strategické cíle výrazně zvyšují napětí v oblasti Rudého moře a Bab al-Mandabu. Současně dochází k nárůstu incidentů v Hormuzském průlivu, kde Írán zesiluje tlak na tankery.
archive.security_status_en: The Saudi-backed offensive in Yemen and escalating Houthi attacks on Aden and strategic targets are significantly heightening tensions in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab strait. Concurrently, incidents are rising in the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran is stepping up pressure on tankers.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat rozsáhlou saúdskoarabskou ofenzívu v Jemenu, na kterou Hútíové odpoví dalšími asymetrickými útoky na lodní dopravu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, a large-scale Saudi-backed offensive in Yemen is expected, prompting asymmetric Houthi retaliations targeting shipping lanes.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se dramaticky vyhrotila po zahájení rozsáhlé saúdskoarabské ofenzívy v Jemenu a vlně útoků na tankery v Perském zálivu i Rudém moři. Ceny ropy prudce vzrostly nad 105 dolarů za barel, zatímco napětí mezi USA a Iránem nadále eskaluje.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region has deteriorated dramatically following the launch of a major Saudi-backed offensive in Yemen and a wave of tanker attacks in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea. Oil prices have surged past $105 per barrel while tensions between the US and Iran continue to escalate.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další stupňování vojenských operací v Jemenu, což povede k přetrvávající vysoké volatilitě cen ropy a rizikům pro námořní trasy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, a further escalation of military operations in Yemen is expected, leading to sustained high volatility in oil prices and risks to shipping lanes.
